questions.text: Unto whom is this epistle written by Paul in Philemon 1:1?

options.text: Unto Archippus our fellowsoldier in the ministry
Unto Philemon dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer
Unto Epaphras, our fellowprisoner in the bonds
Unto Tychicus, our beloved brother and minister

questions.text: In what relation was Onesimus to Philemon before he departed (Philemon 1:11-16)?

options.text: He was a faithful steward over all his earthly estate
He was a natural kinsman dwelling at the city Colosse
He was a servant unto Philemon, in time past unprofitable
He was a foreign merchant that traded with him in goods

questions.explanation: The name Onesimus signifies 'profitable' or 'useful'. Paul plays upon this in Philemon 1:11: which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me.

questions.text: How does Paul describe Onesimus in Philemon 1:10?

options.text: His fellowtraveller whom he took upon all journeys
His scholar whom he instructed in holy scriptures
His messenger whom he sent unto all churches abroad
His son Onesimus, whom he had begotten in his bonds

questions.text: How should Philemon receive Onesimus according to Philemon 1:16?

options.text: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved
Not now as a servant, but as a stranger and hired labourer
Not now as a servant, but as an overseer in the assembly
Not now as a servant, but as a debtor bound unto Caesar

questions.text: What does Paul offer if Onesimus hath wronged Philemon (Philemon 1:18-19)?

options.text: Onesimus must labour many years until all debt be discharged
Put that on Paul's account, and Paul will repay it himself
The whole assembly must gather silver to repay the balance
Philemon must forgive the entire loss without satisfaction
